primitives.name: ECE Bias Correction
primitives.verbatim_quote: ECE has four values in one month — and the "publishable" one is the outlier (P04 §3#3) 0.112 (Aug 9 live audit, RED) → **0.0044** (Aug 19 competitive intel brief, "publishable, FTC-safe") → debiased 0.0374 (Sep 9 PROVEN pool n=380) → 0.0582 (Sep 9 deployed v5.2.7 n=258).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\widehat{\\text{ECE}}_{\\text{raw}}': 'Raw empirical calibration error (dimensionless)', '\\delta': 'Debiasing correction term (dimensionless)', '\\widehat{\\text{ECE}}_{\\text{debias}}': 'Bias-corrected ECE (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Homoscedastic noise distribution, large-sample normal approximation, no overfitting on calibration data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Under-dispersed bins (fewer samples than expected) cause upward bias; zero samples in a bin trigger division by zero.

layer2.mapping: \widehat{\text{ECE}}_{\text{debias}} maps to a conformal coverage error bound after post-processing with isotonic regression. The debiasing step corrects the overestimated miscalibration probability in sparse bins, aligning the empirical coverage with nominal confidence levels. This is analogous to sharpening a non-conformity measure to achieve sharper predictive sets while maintaining valid coverage.
layer2.telemetry: Observed vs. expected frequency in each bin; average absolute difference between predicted probability and actual outcome rate.

primitives.name: Purdy EPA/dropback Percentile Disagreement
primitives.verbatim_quote: Purdy EPA/dropback is 96th percentile, NOT 99th (P05 integrity note) The @xEP_Network transcription reads: 80.4% completion (99th), +14.9 CPOE (99th), +0.63 EPA/dropback (**96th**), 0 sacks taken.
primitives.assumptions: Percentiles are computed from the same reference population (e.g., NFL dropbacks in a given season).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Small sample size (n ≈ 2) leads to high variance in extreme percentiles; slight changes in the reference dataset can shift ranks dramatically.

layer2.mapping: The discrepancy highlights a fundamental duality: raw EPA/dropback (96th) versus composite EPADB metrics (99th). In GSI, this maps to distinguishing between direct empirical outcomes (e.g., yards per attempt) and derived risk-adjusted performance scores. The conflict exposes a failure mode where composite indicators can mask underlying weaknesses in their constituent parts. In GSE, it corresponds to verifying whether a quarterback's immediate situational EPA matches longer-term trajectory models.
layer2.telemetry: Year-over-year rank consistency; comparison of EPADB vs. raw EPA distributions.

primitives.name: Log-Loss Improvement Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: The TacticAI ≥5% log-loss gate is reader-invented, not the paper's (P01 §3F, P05 §1#10) The brief's acceptance gate (≥5% holdout log-loss improvement, paired bootstrap, p<0.05) is the READER'S proposal, not the paper's.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_{\\text{base}}': 'Baseline log-loss (dimensionless)', 'L_{\\text{aug}}': 'Augmented model log-loss (dimensionless)', '\\Delta L': 'Absolute log-loss reduction (percent)', 'p_{\\text{boot}}': 'Paired bootstrap p-value for significance (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Identical test set distribution for both models; independent observations within the bootstrap resamples.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overly aggressive gates (high threshold) lead to false dismissal of useful features; insufficient gate strength invites overfitting to idiosyncratic test splits.

layer2.mapping: The ≥5% log-loss gate functions as a conformal selection rule: it filters augmentations only if they provide statistically significant information gain relative to a simpler baseline. This is mathematically dual to a likelihood ratio test under exponential family losses. In GSI, it maps to feature importance screening; in GSE, it corresponds to deciding whether a new state-transition kernel improves predictive accuracy.
layer2.telemetry: Average log-loss on out-of-sample validation; percentage improvement relative to a reference model.

primitives.name: Minerva Score Seal Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The same document explicitly admits "no peer-reviewed EPA forward-validity study exists" — "v2's biggest literature gap." **Feature weights are being set on an orphan number.** Fix: source the correlation (or measure it from the lab's own filtered sample) before any weight is anchored to it.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{Seal}:': 'Binary validation flag (0 or 1)', '\\text{DSR}:': 'Discrimination stability ratio (dimensionless)', '\\text{PBO}:': 'Proportion below oracle (dimensionless)', '\\text{SPA}:': 'Synthetic AUROC (dimensionless)', 'T:': 'TRL milestone indicator (dimensionless)', '\\rho:': 'Pearson correlation (dimensionless)', '\\text{MinTRL}:': 'Minimum technology readiness level (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: All component metrics are evaluated on independent synthetic data with known ground truth.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Synthetic data does not faithfully replicate real-world distribution shifts; the seal fails when applied to out-of-distribution test sets.

layer2.mapping: The Minerva Score Seal is a \textit{conformal} validity condition: it requires that the model's internal diagnostics (DSR, PBO, SPA) collectively imply reliable calibration on unseen synthetic tasks. The logical AND structure enforces \textit{robustness-by-design}. In GSI, this maps to multi-criteria decision rules for deploying ML pipelines; in GSE, it corresponds to safety-critical state-transition filters.
layer2.telemetry: Synthetic task accuracy; internal diagnostic statistics (DSR, PBO, SPA).

reasoning_traces.think:
Primitive C1 (ECE Bias Correction) is the foundational sovereign operator because it directly addresses the most severe failure mode: wrong numbers. The observed 2-orders-of-magnitude drop from 0.112 to 0.0044 stems from a systematic upward bias in raw empirical calibration error due to sparse bins and pre-debiasing sample selection. The max(0,·) correction removes this bias, yielding a publishable estimate of 0.0374. However, the "publishable" value (0.0044) itself was flawed because it predates the debiasing framework (C-290/C-292) and lacks proper sample labeling. Any public calibration claim must explicitly specify both the sample (e.g., PROVEN pool n=380) and the estimator version (raw vs. debiased). Primitive C2 (Purdy EPA/dropback Percentile Disagreement) reveals a secondary challenge: composite indicators can obscure underlying inconsistencies. Purdy's EPADB metric places Rodgers at the 99th percentile, but his raw EPA/dropback is only at the 96th. This divergence suggests that the composite score may be overweighting certain components. In GSI, this translates into a need for transparent attribution of composite metrics to ensure that no single sub-model dominates the final score. Primitive C3 (Log-Loss Improvement Gate) introduces a third layer: thin samples. The brief proposes a ≥5% log-loss improvement as a filter, but with only n=2 games in the two-week window, the resulting estimates are highly noisy. Noise-rich display-bait metrics cannot serve as reliable engine inputs. The proposed gate is reader-invented rather than intrinsic to the paper, highlighting the need for rigorous statistical testing thresholds. Finally, Primitive C4 (Minerva Score Seal) underscores the fourth challenge: contradictions. The paper's own pre-registered test finds no forward relationship between scores and returns, yet the Minerva Seal still applies a hard logical AND of synthetic diagnostics. This contradiction indicates that internal validation metrics do not guarantee external predictive power. Together, these primitives form a comprehensive diagnostic toolkit for identifying and mitigating the four ranked challenges: wrong numbers, contradictions, thin samples, and lack of forward validity.

reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Cross-layer veto conditions include: (1) \textit{Sample-labeling veto}: Any published result must explicitly cite the exact sample definition and estimator version to prevent misinterpretation. (2) \textit{Forward-validity veto}: Synthetic-seal-only validation does not substitute for real-market forward testing; a model must demonstrate predictive skill on out-of-sample data. (3) \textit{Noise-threshold veto}: Gates based on thin samples (n≪30) are prone to false discoveries and require Bonferroni-style corrections or Bayesian priors to avoid spurious significance. These vetoes ensure that operators are applied only when sufficient empirical evidence supports their use.
